conviction_note: The findings net to a small positive (+0.9): a crowded short (about 15% of shares, 11 days to cover), a low Q3 revenue bar and a new Lilly dispensing deal on one side; a Q4 guide of $60-64m (+25% q/q) that the subscriber trend and the Q2 EBITDA miss make hard to believe, plus a fixed-charge covenant first tested at 30 Sep against negative trailing EBITDA, on the other. The print will turn on whether the Q4/FY guide holds. That is a coin flip on this evidence, so p_up is 50 and abs_move 16 (median past reaction 14.8%, guidance-driven history, crowded short, no option chain), which gives a scaled move of 0. The gap between the sum and the scaled number is the sign uncertainty, not an inconsistency.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide $48-51m and adj. EBITDA -$1m to +$2m (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000948320/000149315226036170/ex99-1.htm). Consensus is revenue $48.80m and EPS -$0.14 (MarketBeat preview 2026-11-02, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-lifemd-lfmd-set-to-announce-earnings-on-monday-2026-11-02/), so consensus sits at the bottom of the guide. Before the guide, Q3 consensus was $58.55m (TheFly via stockanalysis), so it has been reset. Forward bar: Q4 guide $60-64m, adj. EBITDA $3-6m; FY $205.5-212.5m, adj. EBITDA -$6m to 0. The estimate side has one aggregator; the company guide anchors the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 7.4M shares, ~15.3% of shares outstanding, 11.0 days to cover, down 2.1% month on month (equibles.com, page read 2026-11-06; settlement date not shown, https://equibles.com/stocks/lfmd). findings.finding: The company's own Q4 2026 guide ($60-64m revenue, +21-29% over Q3's $48-51m guide; adj. EBITDA $3-6m, implying a ~$250m exit run rate) needs a sharp step-up. Its own numbers show momentum going the other way: active subscribers fell from ~365,000 at Q1 (8-K, May 2026) to ~356,000 at Q2. Q2 adj. EBITDA of -$3.5m came in below its own -$2m to +$1m guide. The FY guide was already cut once, from $220-230m to $205.5-212.5m. A second cut, or a Q4 trim on Nov 9, is the main downside path. The stock at $2.27 against analyst targets of $5-9 suggests the market already doubts the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has driven this name: 2025-08-05 -44.85% (guide cut), 2026-08-05 -7.61% (FY cut, Q3 guide below consensus), 2026-05-06 -14.8%, 2025-11-17 -13.53%; 2026-03-09 +25.32% on a Q4 beat and FY guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down 57% from its high and 13.5% over 20 days, which looks like doubt about the H2 ramp. But the sell side has not reset (8 Buy, targets $5-9, B. Riley re-initiated at Buy in early October). The FY consensus EPS of -$0.48 still embeds the Q4 step-up. If a cut were fully expected, targets would be lower and short interest would not still be rising toward 11 days to cover.
findings.independence: Subscriber counts come from the Q1 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000948320/000149315226021520/ex99-1.htm), a different document from the Q2 release. The Q2 EBITDA miss against guide is in the same two documents. Both are company documents, so this is one finding, not two.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-05, two trading days before the print, LifeMD announced that its own licensed mail-order pharmacy can now dispense and ship Lilly's self-pay Zepbound and Foundayo nationwide at Lilly's self-pay prices. That moves branded GLP-1 fulfilment from LillyDirect/Gifthealth into LifeMD's pharmacy, which supports the 'higher pharmacy attachment' driver of the Q4 step-up the company cited. The release gave no revenue figures.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold its own partnership news: -6.4% on 2026-11-05, the day of this release (2.45 to 2.29), after +12% the day before; after the 2026-09-15 AT&T release it rose to $3.22 and has since fallen 30%. Previous GLP-1 pricing and access news (Novo price cut, Nov 2025) gave about +5.8% premarket and did not hold.
findings.why_not_priced: The release has no numbers, and the stock fell on the day, so the market gave it nothing. If management uses it on Nov 9 to firm the Q4 guide or quantify pharmacy revenue, that would be new. If the market had priced it as a guide support, the Nov 5 close would not sit below the Nov 3 level ($2.18 to $2.29 net, after a round trip).
findings.independence: Also carried on Yahoo Finance and Manila Times reprints of the same GlobeNewswire release (https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/lifemd-expands-access-lilly-self-123000327.html). Same document; no independent quantification.

findings.finding: AT&T (2026-09-15 8-K exhibit 99.1) made LifeMD its exclusive virtual-care partner. The $19/month membership is waived for eligible wireless and fiber customers: 29m customers in 11 states at launch, more than 100m eligible, more states in January 2027. Visits are paid ($29/$49/$79). The Q3 revenue effect is negligible because only two weeks fall in the quarter, but Q3 is the first quarter in which management can give enrolment numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose to $3.22 by 2026-09-18 on the announcement and then gave all of it back ($2.27 now). Enterprise partnership news has not held on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The announcement itself is priced and round-tripped. What is not public is any enrolment or conversion figure. A strong number on the call would be new; if the market were holding any expectation for it, the stock would not have fully given back the September move.
findings.independence: The Wainwright note of 2026-09-17 (Buy, $9) commented on the partnership (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-lifemd-lfmd-set-to-announce-earnings-on-monday-2026-11-02/). This is sell-side colour, not independent data.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q shows that the June 30, 2026 waiver of the Citizens Bank $30m revolver (undrawn) replaced the interest-coverage test, which the company had failed at 3/31/26. The new tests, starting with the quarter ending 9/30/2026, are a Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio of at least 1.25x and Cash on Hand plus Unused Availability of at least $40m. Adj. EBITDA was -$4.5m in Q1 and -$3.5m in Q2, and the Q3 guide is -$1m to +$2m, so a trailing fixed-charge test looks hard to pass without pro-forma add-backs; definitions are not disclosed. Cash was $25.1m (from $36.8m at YE25), working capital was -$4.5m, and the 12-month sufficiency statement relies on ATM proceeds, with $44.6m of ATM capacity left. On the money question, the facility funds no visible ramp; it is a liquidity backstop under covenant pressure, so the sign is negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned visibly on financing. The March 2026 covenant breach was disclosed in the Q1 10-Q alongside a -14.8% reaction driven by operations.
findings.why_not_priced: The covenant sits in a 10-Q note, not the press release, and no aggregator carries it. No 8-K (item 1.01 or 2.04) has been filed since August, so a second waiver, if any, would first appear in the Q3 10-Q or release. If priced, short interest would not be falling slightly and the analysts would have flagged liquidity. The crowded short shrinks this.
findings.independence: The cash decline and the ATM reliance come from the same 10-Q. The S-8 filed 2026-09-25 (EDGAR submissions, https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000948320.json) is employee-plan registration, not an equity raise. No independent source; this is covenant arithmetic.

findings.finding: Positioning: about 7.4M shares short, ~15.3% of shares outstanding and 11.0 days to cover on a 20-day average volume of 662k (baseline). Market cap is ~$110m and short volume was 64% on 2026-11-05. An in-line print or a held Q4 guide meets an 11-day cover queue, so a squeeze is a mechanism of its own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-03-09 +25.32% and 2025-03-10 +30.68% were up moves of that size on this name when the print cleared the bar. Short interest was 12-13% of float in 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is in the price only as pressure. The squeeze option is not priced in a way that can be read: the option chain is unusable (100% ATM spread), so no skew shows what the market pays for upside. If the short were already covering, days to cover would be falling fast, not easing 2%.
findings.independence: The July 2026 snapshot of 5.9M short, 12.1%, 6.6 days (equibles via search, https://equibles.com/stocks/lfmd/summary) shows the short building into the print. Same aggregator.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar is low: consensus of $48.8m sits at the bottom of the $48-51m guide. The company beat its Q1 revenue range ($50.2m against $48-49m) and landed at the low end in Q2 ($47.3m against $47-50m). A Q3 number inside the guide is what the company told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue inside the guide but below the $49.16m consensus, plus an EBITDA miss, gave -7.61%. Q1 2026: a revenue beat with the FY reaffirmed gave -14.8%. Reported-quarter revenue alone has not decided the move here; guidance has.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: this is inside the guide. The small residual is that consensus sits below the guide midpoint ($49.5m), so a midpoint print is a nominal beat.
findings.independence: The guide is in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000948320/000149315226036170/ex99-1.htm) and the Q1 beat in the Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000948320/000149315226021520/ex99-1.htm).
